problem: How many different arrangements of gold, silver, and bronze medalists can there be out of $10$ Olympic athletes, assuming there are no ties?
worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $10$ athletes, so $n=10.$ We want to select $3$ of those athletes to receive gold, silver, or bronze medals, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different ways to award the medals is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{P}_{3} & =\frac{10!}{(10-3)!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{7!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}} \\  & =10\cdot 9\cdot 8 \\  & =720.\end{aligned}
$$
